verdict.rationale: Crossplane's core model is exposing declarative, Kubernetes-native APIs that 'humans, automation, and AI systems can safely act on', and it 'works with all the Kubernetes tools you already use'. So deployments can be driven by API-calling automation rather than only the CLI. However, the evidence never documents a client SDK, application-code examples, or how a developer invokes these APIs from their own code; that part is only implied. Missing for 10: documented client libraries or SDKs, code examples of creating or updating composite resources from application code, and hands-on corroboration of programmatic driving.

support.subject: As a developer, I can drive deployments programmatically from my own application code rather than only through the CLI

citations.quote: Expose declarative APIs that humans, automation, and AI systems can safely act on
enable consumers, whether human users, automated workflows, or AI agents, to self-service
It's built on Kubernetes, so it works with all the Kubernetes tools you already use.
declarative APIs that make intent explicit, auditable, and and machine-readable
